topic: Why plane windows are round (de Havilland Comet, 1954)
taste: Two Comet breakups in 1954 killed everyone aboard: show only a cartoon plane's metal cracking, never people, fire or a crash.

claims.claim: The de Havilland Comet was the first jet airliner (in service 1952) and had squarish windows.
Pressurising the cabin on every flight (and releasing it after) loads the fuselage metal again and again (metal fatigue).
Stress concentrates at sharp window corners, much more than engineers expected.
Fatigue cracks led to two Comets breaking apart in flight in 1954.
Rounded/oval windows let stress flow around the opening with no corner peak, which is why airliner windows are round today.
After the inquiry the redesigned Comet (Comet 4, 1958) got oval/rounded windows and a thicker skin; airliners have used rounded windows since.
